[[Wing Commander]] '''Charles Angas Hurst''' (22 September 1923 – 19 October 2011<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.onlinetributes.com.au/Charles_Hurst|title=Death notice|website=www.onlinetributes.com.au|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111116203041/http://www.onlinetributes.com.au/Charles_Hurst|archive-date=16 November 2011}}</ref><ref>https://science.org.au/our-focus/history-australian-science/conversations-australian-scientists/professor-angas-hurst-mathematical-physicist</ref>) was an Australian [[mathematical physicist]] noted for his work in lattice models, [[quantum field theory]], [[asymptotic expansions]] and [[Lie groups]]. He was appointed a [[Member of the Order of Australia]] in 2003, elected a [[Fellow of the Australian Academy of Science]] in 1972, and awarded the [[Centenary Medal]] and an Hon DSc (Melb).<ref name=AM>{{cite web |title= Member of the Order of Australia |date= 26 January 2003 |quote= For service to science, particularly in the field of mathematical physics as an educator, researcher and administrator |publisher= It's an Honour |url= https://honours.pmc.gov.au/honours/awards/1042205 }}</ref><ref name=CM>{{cite web |title= Centenary Medal |date= 1 January 2001 |quote= For service to Australian society and science in mathematical physics |publisher= It's an Honour |url= https://honours.pmc.gov.au/honours/awards/1127237 }}</ref>

His PhD was a seminal work on quantum field theory, developing asymptotic expansions for perturbation expansions. In 1952 Hurst represented Australia in the inaugural [[International Mathematical Union]].{{citation needed|date=June 2020}}

Hurst's work with [[Herbert S. Green|Herbert Green]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.science.org.au/academy/memoirs/green.htm |title=AAS-Biographical memoirs-Green |publisher=Science.org.au |date= |accessdate=2008-11-07 |archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20080722141012/http://science.org.au/academy/memoirs/green.htm <!-- Bot retrieved archive --> |archivedate = 2008-07-22}}</ref> on lattice problems and the [[Ising model]] led to the Free fermion field model,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://scitation.aip.org/getabs/servlet/GetabsServlet?prog=normal&id=JCPSA6000033000004001059000001&idtype=cvips&gifs=yes|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120718203613/http://scitation.aip.org/getabs/servlet/GetabsServlet?prog=normal&id=JCPSA6000033000004001059000001&idtype=cvips&gifs=yes|url-status=dead|archive-date=18 July 2012|title=Home Page|work=[[American Institute of Physics]]|accessdate=22 August 2015}}</ref> which contained all known properties of [[Fermions]] at the time of its publication.  Hurst's work with Thirring ([[Thirring model]]) found the simplest non-linear field and is still used as a test model for [[Perturbation theory (quantum mechanics)|perturbation theory]].{{citation needed|date=June 2020}}

Hurst served as acting [[vice-chancellor]] of the [[University of Adelaide]] in 1985, relieving Donald (Don) Stranks.<ref> https://archive.austms.org.au/Publ/Gazette/2012/Mar12/ObitHurst.pdf</ref>
